bg.purpose: The day desk: page, tabs, inputs, open menus, the Interrupt key, the toast and a reply table's sticky column.

card.purpose: One step off the ground: buttons, ref chips, code, reply table heads and the console box.

hover.purpose: Hover fill of buttons, tray items, menu summaries and menu rows.

line.purpose: Every border and rule: between dispatches and rows, the masthead edge, the tab rule, slug separators, quote edges and scrollbars.

fg.purpose: Body copy, titles, routine wire codes, the print head and the current tab.

muted.purpose: Slugs, meta, hints, service lines, the working line, inactive tabs, placeholders, field labels, crumbs and quotes.

primary.purpose: Fill of the one committing button in a form: Answer, Send, Resume.

flash.purpose: The one saturated signal: FLASH and URGENT codes, failing and blocked states, the Interrupt key, the toast border.

fail.purpose: The failing-check icon, stuck reports and the toast border; same value as flash.

wait.purpose: BULLETIN, waiting tasks, progress reports, the waiting count, Queued and a pending switch.

pass.purpose: Running and passing tasks, and done reports.

neutral.purpose: The idle-check icon; same value as muted.

pencil.purpose: The operator's marks: your notes' slug and 1px rule, and the console frame on focus.

accent.purpose: Links, the focus ring, the caret, a linked ref on hover, the PR chip and the Chat tab's working dot.

wait-bg.purpose: The non-zero waiting count and the arrival wash of a new tray item.

on-header-muted.purpose: The word Wire, the fleet id, strip details, the clock and Notify.

h-wait.purpose: The gauge at 80% and the stale-server note; theme-invariant.

h-flash.purpose: A failing lamp and the gauge at 90%; theme-invariant.

screen.purpose: Ground of a blocked supervisor screen; dark in both themes.

screen-fg.purpose: Text of a blocked supervisor screen.

shadow.purpose: The toast lift and the Interrupt key's depressed inset.

nameplate-compact.purpose: The nameplate in the 36px compact masthead on viewports under 600px tall; still large text, so every tint clears 3:1.

headline.purpose: Task and decision titles on thread pages, balanced.

title.purpose: The tray headline; 500 and truncated when the item is collapsed.

section.purpose: The Checks head and a reply's top-level heading.

heading-small.purpose: A reply's lower headings and the fleet list's heading.

copy.purpose: Dispatch copy on the wire, reports, plans and goals; prose capped at 72ch.

body.purpose: Everything else: budget rows, tray bodies, inputs.

control.purpose: Buttons and menu rows; crumbs share the size at 400.

meta.purpose: Hints, meta text, the service line's frame and the finished-tasks link.

badge.purpose: The PR chip and reply table heads; the waiting count on a 20px line.

label.purpose: The outlined Queued label in a note's slug.

slug.purpose: Every slug line: items separated by a trailing middle dot in hairline colour.

wire-code.purpose: FLASH, BULLETIN, URGENT, ROUTINE and SERVICE at the head of a slug.

strip.purpose: The masthead live strip and the clock; the line word at 700, details at 500.

key-label.purpose: The tabs, the model menu summary, the plain model label and the pending switch.

field-label.purpose: Profile, Model and Effort labels in the model menu.

mono.purpose: Ref chips, service text, the working line and the fleet id; own case.

keycap.purpose: The Ctrl or Command Enter keycap beside Send.

code-block.purpose: The blocked-screen excerpt and preformatted text.

shadows.name: toast-lift
shadows.purpose: The error toast, the one element that floats over the page.

shadows.name: keycap-edge
shadows.purpose: Bottom edge of each key in a blocked screen's key fence.

shadows.name: depressed-key
shadows.purpose: The Interrupt key, shown only while the turn runs, so always pressed in.

shadows.name: focus-frame
shadows.purpose: With a pencil border, the console box's 2px frame while the message box has focus; a focus state, not depth.

motion.name: print-head
motion.purpose: The one authored motion: a .62em by 1.05em ink block steps along the working line and returns like a teleprinter carriage; static at the line's start under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: feed
motion.purpose: A dispatch with a new number rises one line into the wire; none under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: lamp
motion.purpose: The masthead lamp while the supervisor works; steady under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: arrive
motion.purpose: A new tray item washes from amber to its ground; none under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: app-shell
breakpoints.purpose: With body[data-page=fleet][data-shell]: the body fills 100dvh and never scrolls; #needs and the wire scroll on their own; the message box stops at 40dvh.

breakpoints.name: short
breakpoints.purpose: A 36px sticky compact masthead (nameplate 19px; fleet id, clock and Notify hidden), tabs sticky at 36px, the console box sticky at the bottom, the page scrolling as one, the message box stopping at 30dvh.

breakpoints.name: tabs-wide
breakpoints.purpose: Tabs take their content width at 10px by 14px, starting at the column's left edge.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Board padding 12px; a two-row masthead (nameplate and bell, then strip and clock); the fleet id and the budget rows' attempt hidden; the console hint on its own row; tabs split into halves.

breakpoints.name: coarse-pointer
breakpoints.purpose: 16px inputs, selects and text areas; the Send keycap hidden.

breakpoints.name: reduced-motion
breakpoints.purpose: The print head, the feed, the lamp pulse and the arrival wash stop.

containers.name: column
containers.purpose: Every block in #needs and #chat, centred; the tab bar pads by max(16px, (100% - 880px) / 2) and the wire by max(2px, (100% - 880px) / 2).

containers.name: board
containers.purpose: The fleet page's board spans the window, so panels scroll from the gutter.

containers.name: thread
containers.purpose: Task, decision, conversation, fleet list and error pages; padded 20px 16px 48px with a 14px gap.

containers.name: prose
containers.purpose: Dispatch and note prose; tables and code blocks may run to the column.

containers.name: note
containers.purpose: The widest a note runs, flush right on the wire.

containers.name: menu
containers.purpose: Minimum width of the model menu's form.

layers.name: console-box
layers.purpose: The sticky console box on the flowing page, above sticky table cells.

layers.name: compact-masthead
layers.purpose: The sticky masthead on short viewports.

icons.forbidden: Octicons, any icon package or font, and Unicode glyphs standing in for icons
icons.chevron: One downward stroke beside the model menu; turns 180deg when the menu opens.

fleetTint.algorithm: FNV-1a 32 of the fleet id, mod 12; empty id gives 0
fleetTint.class: body.tint-N (and li.fleet.tint-N on the fleet list) sets --tint
uses: the fleet name in the masthead nameplate
fleetTint.fleetListName: ink at rest, the tint on hover; tints reach about 3.4:1 on canary

constraints.csp: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'
constraints.fonts: No font-src; TestNoWebFonts rejects @font-face and url( in board.css
constraints.liveUpdates: Server-Sent Events; app.js swaps a region's HTML whole, keeping drafts, open details, focus and a pinned wire
constraints.withoutJs: Every control is a POST and redirect; menus are details elements; both panels show; datelines stay UTC

gauge.format: CTX 508K, or CTX 1.2M from 1,000,000; three significant figures

strip.threadPages: a static copy with no data-region

datelines.dispatch: local month, day, 24-hour time and short zone, e.g. SEP 29, 22:22 GMT+7
datelines.clock: local 24-hour HH:MM without zone; the zone in its tooltip; updated every 30 s
datelines.withoutJs: server UTC, Jan 2 15:04, and an empty clock

wire.dispatchSlug: ref of the supervisor live when the entry was written · NO. n (1-based transcript position) · dateline
wire.note: YOU · dateline, in pencil; flush right at up to 80%; 12px in from a 1px pencil rule
wire.serviceLine: HAND · dateline, then the event in mono in its own case
workingLine: sN is working · 4m, on your message from HH:MM
sN is working · 4m, on a wake
sN is working · 4m, since it started
wire.refs: tN, dN, aN and rN in supervisor copy link through <base>/ref/<ref>; refs inside code and links stay plain

console.modelMenu: details#model-menu: profile (running harness only), model, effort; Switch now when ready, Switch after this turn otherwise
console.pendingSwitch: target model and effort in amber Key Label caps, with Cancel
console.interrupt: a 32 by 28px depressed key with a FLASH-red solid square, while working and not blocked
console.moreMenu: details#more-menu: Stop; New session and Other harness once ended

composerHints.ready: sN is ready; it reads your message now.
composerHints.working: sN is working; your message goes to it right away.
composerHints.blocked: sN is waiting on a screen in Needs you; your message waits too.
composerHints.switch pending: sN switches to M E after this turn; your message waits for the new session.
composerHints.launching: sN is starting; your message waits.
composerHints.none: No supervisor is running; your message waits until one starts.
composerHints.unreachable: Luvus restarted; your message waits until hand watch settles it.

console.network: no console box on a network listener

labels: Needs you, with the waiting count
Chat, with a static 6px accent dot while the supervisor works
tabs.current: ink text and a 2px ink underline
tabs.initial: The URL hash (#needs or #chat), else needs when something waits, else chat.
tabs.auto: The board never switches tabs by itself.
tabs.withoutJs: Both panels show; the tabs are in-page anchors.

favicons.whyLiteral: Presentation attributes in fixed mid-tones: a static SVG under the strict CSP cannot read the page's custom properties or follow its theme.
favicons.choice: attention when something waits or the agent is blocked; working when the agent is working; plain otherwise
favicons.title: (N) fleet when something waits, ● fleet while the supervisor works, fleet otherwise

departures.why: Reads as one more hairline, not a coloured stripe.
15px is not a step on the ramp.

departures.spec: each fleet's wire name in its tint
departures.build: the name in ink, the mark tinted
no shadow on the sticky console box
departures.why: Only the floating toast and honest keys carry shadows.
The lamp's colours belong to the ink band.

narrative.overview:
The fleet runs like a news agency wire desk, and the operator edits the desk. Every event is a dispatch ranked by wire priority. What waits on the operator sits in the tray, FLASH first, each item with its action in place. The tasks are the news budget, one line each. The supervisor's replies come over the wire as numbered dispatches. Hand's own events are one-line service messages, and the operator's notes sit flush right in blue editor's pencil. While the supervisor works, a print head steps along the wire's last line, and the masthead counts its context.

The material is teleprinter copy: canary on the day desk, carbon on the night desk, near-black ink, and an ink masthead band in both themes. Rank comes from scale, weight and caps on one slug grid, never from boxes. Dispatches are separated by 1px hairlines, with no cards, no glass and no zebra. FLASH red is the one saturated signal. Fixed-pitch caps carry what the wire prints: slugs, refs, codes, datelines, counts, the live strip and the tabs. Copy stays in the system sans.

The desk refuses chat bubbles in a SaaS shell, and it refuses the green-on-black terminal as well. Every page shows one fleet. The fleet page keeps two tabs at every width, Needs you and Chat, each over one centred 880px column, and the send console sits under the wire as a single box.
keyCharacteristics: Canary copy (day) and carbon (night) grounds under near-black ink, with the masthead an ink band in both themes.
One dispatch module everywhere: a mono-caps slug line, then the copy, then its actions, with hairlines between dispatches.
Wire codes rank the tray: FLASH, BULLETIN, URGENT, ROUTINE, SERVICE.
FLASH red is the one saturated signal; pencil blue marks the operator's words and focus; the fleet tint colours only the wire name and the mark.
A live strip in the masthead: lamp, line state, supervisor and model, queue, context gauge, compactions and clock.
One authored motion, the print head, plus a one-line feed for new dispatches.
A send console that holds the message box, the model menu, the Interrupt key, the overflow menu, the hint and Send.
Shadows only on the floating toast and on honest keys.
A strict CSP: one stylesheet, one script, no inline code and no web fonts.

rules.name: The One Flash Rule
rules.body: FLASH red is the one saturated signal: blocked screens, failures, the Interrupt key and a context gauge at 90% or more. Amber means the operator is being asked or something waits, and green means running, passing or ready. There is no fourth signal colour. Pencil blue marks the operator and focus, and the fleet tint never carries state.

rules.name: The Ink Band Rule
rules.body: The masthead is an ink band in both themes and has its own tokens: `on-header` and `on-header-muted` for text, and the `h-` set for signals. Band tokens stay on the band, and ground tokens stay on the ground.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: In both themes, `fail`, `flash`, `wait`, `pass`, `neutral`, `fg`, `muted` and `pencil` reach 4.5:1 on `bg` and on `card`. `on-header`, `on-header-muted` and every `h-` signal reach 4.5:1 on `header`, and every tint reaches 3:1 on `header`. `TestColoursMeetContrast` in `internal/board/identity_test.go` enforces all three, and `TestTheWireDeskTokens` checks that the day ground is canary and the night ground is carbon.

rules.name: The Tint Is a Name Rule
rules.body: The fleet tint colours only the wire name in the masthead and the mark. On the fleet list the rows sit on canary, where the tints reach only about 3.4:1, so the name stays in ink and only the mark takes the tint. A departure from the spec, which tinted the name there too.

rules.name: The Slug Rule
rules.body: A slug line is mono caps (11.5px/18px at .03em) on one baseline row. Its items are separated by a trailing "·" in hairline colour, so the separator stays at the end of a line when the slug wraps. Every item is data: a wire code, a kind, a ref, a source, a dispatch number, a state or a dateline. A slug that only names a topic is a kicker, and the desk has none.

rules.name: The Mono Carries Data Rule
rules.body: Mono is for what the wire prints or the operator could type. That covers slugs, refs, codes, datelines, counts, the live strip, the clock and the tabs. It also covers the model menu with its field labels, the Queued label, keys and terminal text. Titles, copy, command buttons, hints and links stay in the sans.

rules.name: The Dateline Rule
rules.body: Datelines are 24-hour and carry the zone: `app.js` rewrites each one as local month, day, hour and minute with the short zone name, and the slug sets it in caps ("SEP 29, 22:22 GMT+7"). The masthead clock and the working line's "from" time are 24-hour without the zone. The clock names the zone in its tooltip. Without JavaScript, datelines stay in the server's UTC form ("SEP 29 15:19") and the clock is empty.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Times, counts, meta, refs, the gauge, the clock, dispatch numbers and reply tables all use tabular figures, so that live numbers do not jitter.

rules.name: The Region Rule
rules.body: Live content lives in exactly five fleet-page regions: `status` (the masthead live strip), `console` (the console's controls), `timeline`, `queue` and `tasks`. Each has a `data-region` attribute. The server sends each region's HTML over Server-Sent Events, and `app.js` swaps the region whole. The swap keeps typed drafts, open or closed details, focus, and a wire pinned to its newest dispatch. `#composer` and `#toast` stay outside every region: the composer form and the console region sit side by side inside `.console-box`, and neither form nests in the other. `TestFirstViewportOrder` enforces the order status, needs, queue, tasks, chat, timeline, composer, console. The task page is one `task` region. Other thread pages carry a static copy of the strip, which belongs to no region.

rules.name: The Clear-In-Place Rule
rules.body: The first tray item stands alone and open, with its action in its body. The rest share one ruled list, collapsed to one line each, and open in place.

rules.name: The Hands-Off Tabs Rule
rules.body: The board opens on the tab that the URL hash names. With no hash, it opens on Needs you when something waits, and on Chat otherwise. A click on a tab writes its hash with `history.replaceState`. Nothing else changes the tab. A new waiting item raises the count, the title and the favicon, but never pulls the operator out of Chat.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose in a dispatch and in a note stops at 72ch. Tables and code blocks may run wider, up to the column, and scroll sideways past it.

rules.name: The Flat Desk Rule
rules.body: Resting surfaces carry a 1px hairline and no shadow. The sticky console box and the open menus have none either. `TestTheWireDeskTokens` fails on any `box-shadow` outside the console box's focus frame, the menus, the toast, the key fence, the Interrupt key and the keycap. The spec allowed a lift under the sticky composer; the build dropped it.

dos: Do take every colour from a custom property on `:root` in `board.css`, and give each new property a value in the `prefers-color-scheme:dark` block too, unless it lives on the ink band.
Do keep signals at 4.5:1 on `bg` and `card`, band text and `h-` signals at 4.5:1 on `header`, and tints at 3:1 on `header`, in both themes; `TestColoursMeetContrast` checks all three.
Do build every new item as a dispatch: a slug line of data in mono caps, the copy, then its actions, with a 1px hairline to the next.
Do rank with scale, weight and caps: 22px for nameplates and thread titles, 16px for tray headlines and section heads, 14.5px for wire copy, and the slug line at 11.5px.
Do keep FLASH red for blocked screens, failures, the Interrupt key and a gauge at 90% or more, amber for what asks or waits, and green for running, passing or ready.
Do mark the operator's own words and the console's focus in pencil blue.
Do cap prose at 72ch, and let tables and code blocks run to the column.
Do put live content in one of the five regions, `status`, `console`, `timeline`, `queue` or `tasks`, and keep `#composer` and `#toast` outside every region.
Do draw new icons as Hand's own inline SVG in `icons.html`, on a 16px viewBox, with `aria-hidden="true"` and one to four paths.
Do open menus upward from the console as `details` elements with no shadow, so that every control still works as a POST without JavaScript.
Do stop every motion under `prefers-reduced-motion`: the print head, the feed, the lamp's pulse and the tray's arrival wash.
Do lay out for both scenes with the paired height queries: the app shell at `(min-height:600px)` under `body[data-shell]`, and the flowing page at `(max-height:599px)` or without `data-shell`.
donts: Don't add inline script, a `<style>` element, a `style=` attribute, `@font-face` or `url(` in the stylesheet. The CSP is `default-src 'none'` with `script-src 'self'` and `style-src 'self'`, and the board tests reject each of these.
Don't put an item in a card, a glass panel or a zebra row; hairlines and type carry rank.
Don't add a shadow outside the toast and the keys; `TestTheWireDeskTokens` fails on any other `box-shadow`.
Don't put a topic label above a heading; a slug line carries only data.
Don't set copy, titles, command buttons, hints or links in mono; only a key's own legend is set in mono.
Don't use the fleet tint anywhere but the masthead's wire name and the mark, and don't let it carry state.
Don't put band tokens (`on-header`, `on-header-muted`, `h-`) on the canary or carbon ground, or ground tokens on the band.
Don't add a fourth signal colour, or let pencil blue mark a task, a waiting item or an outcome.
Don't use Octicons, an icon package, an icon font, or a Unicode glyph standing in for an icon on the page.
Don't bring back the two-column grid or a `min-width:900px` split; `TestTheAppShellNeedsHeight` rejects it.
Don't switch tabs for the operator; only the URL hash, the opening rule and a click choose the panel.
Don't remove `[hidden]{display:none!important}`; the tabs rely on it to hide the other panel.
